name: Linet-Tian Static Cylinder
description: The static vacuum field with cylindrical symmetry and a cosmological constant, the field outside an infinitely long straight line of mass, which Bernard Linet and Qingjun Tian found independently in 1986. With a negative constant it approaches anti-de Sitter space far from its axis; with a positive one the proper distance from the axis is bounded by $\pi/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$, and the surfaces of constant distance are tori.
convention: The exponents $p_0$, $p_2$ and $p_3$ are those of Levi-Civita's cylinder in proper distance, with $p_0 + p_2 + p_3 = p_0^2 + p_2^2 + p_3^2 = 1$, and every component assumes both conditions. We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: The static vacuum around an infinitely long straight line of mass, in a universe with a cosmological constant $\Lambda$, depends only on the proper distance $\rho$ from the axis. Its line element is $ds^2 = d\rho^2 + Q^{2/3}\left(-P^{2p_t}c^2dt^2 + P^{2p_z}dz^2 + P^{2p_\phi}d\phi^2/C^2\right)$, where $Q = \sin(\sqrt{3\Lambda}\,\rho)/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$ and $P = 2\tan(\sqrt{3\Lambda}\,\rho/2)/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$ [dasilva2000, zofka2008]. The exponents are $p_t = -(4\sigma^2 - 8\sigma + 1)/(3\Sigma)$, $p_z = (8\sigma^2 - 4\sigma - 1)/(3\Sigma)$, and $p_\phi = -2(2\sigma^2 + 2\sigma - 1)/(3\Sigma)$, where $\Sigma = 4\sigma^2 - 2\sigma + 1$ [dasilva2000]. Near the axis and as $\Lambda \to 0$ both $Q$ and $P$ tend to $\rho$, and the metric becomes the static cylinder of Tullio Levi-Civita, with $\sigma$ his mass parameter and $C$ its conicity [dasilva2000, griffiths2010linettian]. For a negative $\Lambda$ the sine and the tangent become hyperbolic functions of $\sqrt{3|\Lambda|}\,\rho$ [dasilva2000, zofka2008]. With $\Lambda \neq 0$ the Weyl tensor vanishes for no member, so de Sitter and anti-de Sitter space, which are conformally flat, are not among them [dasilva2000, griffiths2010linettian].¶Bernard Linet in Paris and Qingjun Tian in Chicago found these solutions independently, each to describe the field outside a cosmic string [zofka2008, linet1986, tian1986]. Linet's paper was received in October 1985 and Tian's that December [linet1986, tian1986]. Tian wrote that "all static and cylindrically symmetric vacuum solutions of Einstein's field equation with cosmological constant" are found [tian1986]. Andrzej Krasiński had given empty space fields with a cosmological constant in 1975, as exteriors for a rotating perfect fluid, with a cross term between time and the angle about the axis [krasinski1975]. Reinaldo Gleiser showed in 2021 that one of Krasiński's four types becomes static under a linear change of its Killing vectors and is then the Linet-Tian family [gleiser2021krasinski, krasinski1975]. Krasiński had left the static case aside, writing that the generalisation of the static vacuum to a nonzero $\Lambda$ is "unexpectedly very involved" [krasinski1975].¶With a negative constant the metric is regular everywhere away from the axis, and far from it every member approaches anti-de Sitter space in horospherical coordinates [zofka2008, dasilva2000, tian1986]. Its axis is singular for every $\sigma$ except $0$ and $1/2$, as in Levi-Civita's field [dasilva2000]. Martin Žofka and Jiří Bičák built nonsingular cylindrical shells as sources of the field in 2008 [zofka2008]. With $\Lambda < 0$, $\sigma = 0$, and $C = 1$ the axis is regular too, and the spacetime has no singularity anywhere [bronnikov2020, sarioglu2009comment]. William Bonnor described this member in 2008 as a second anti-de Sitter universe, "static, cylindrically symmetric and of Petrov class D" [bonnor2008second]. Özgür Sarıoğlu and Bayram Tekin identified it with the soliton of anti-de Sitter space found by Gary Horowitz and Robert Myers, through a change of radius that Roberto Emparan suggested [sarioglu2009comment, horowitz1998].¶A positive constant gives $\rho$ a finite range, from $0$ to $\pi/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$, and the far end is a second curvature singularity unless $\sigma$ is $-1/2$, $1/4$, or $1$ [dasilva2000, griffiths2010linettian]. Jerry Griffiths and Jiří Podolský showed in 2010 that $z$ is then periodic like $\phi$, so every surface of constant $\rho$ is a torus, and each singular end is a closed axis with its own conicity [griffiths2010linettian]. They replaced one singular axis with a toroidal region of the Einstein static universe full of dust, matched to the vacuum across a torus [griffiths2010linettian]. The dust then has a mass per unit length of $\sigma(1 - \sigma)/(1 - 4\sigma^2)$, approximately $\sigma$ for small values [griffiths2010linettian]. Reflected about the middle of the range of $\rho$, with $\phi$ and $z$ exchanged and $C = 1$, the metric with $\sigma$ becomes the one with $(1 - 4\sigma)/(4(1 - \sigma))$, so its far axis carries a source of that strength [griffiths2010linettian]. For a positive constant Tian found three exteriors of a string: a universe with a curvature singularity, one with a conical singularity, and one with no singularity [tian1986].¶Every member with $\Lambda \neq 0$ is of Petrov type I except those with $\sigma = -1/2$, $0$, $1/4$, $1/2$, and $1$, which are of type D and carry a fourth Killing vector [dasilva2000]. At $\sigma = 0$ that vector is a boost along the axis, and at $\sigma = \pm 1/2$ it is a rotation in the plane of $z$ and $\phi$, which gives those two members plane symmetry [dasilva2000, zofka2008]. With $\Lambda < 0$ the surface $\rho = 0$ of the member with $\sigma = 1/2$ is a horizon, and Žofka and Bičák transformed that member into the static, uncharged black string of José Lemos [dasilva2000, zofka2008, lemos1995]. Griffiths and Podolský found the member with $\sigma = 0$ to be a generalisation of the B III metric with a cosmological constant, among the solutions of Jerzy Plebański and Marek Demiański without expansion [griffiths2010linettian]. Gleiser found unstable modes of gravitational perturbations with a negative constant in 2017, for a large set of boundary conditions [gleiser2017stability]. With a positive constant he established the linear instability of the family in 2021 [gleiser2021perturbations].

related.text: At $\Lambda = 0$ both functions of the line element are the proper distance $\rho$, and the field is Tullio Levi-Civita's cylinder with $\sigma$ his mass parameter [dasilva2000, griffiths2010linettian].

With $\Lambda < 0$, $\sigma = 0$, and $C = 1$ the axis is regular and the field is the soliton of anti-de Sitter space, which William Bonnor called a second anti-de Sitter universe [sarioglu2009comment, bonnor2008second].

At $\Lambda = 0$ and $\sigma = 0$ the field is flat with an angular deficit about the axis, the cosmic string that Bernard Linet and Qingjun Tian set in a universe with a cosmological constant [griffiths2010linettian, zofka2008].
The flat member of these holes, the static black string of José Lemos, is the field with $\sigma = 1/2$ and $\Lambda < 0$, its horizon at $\rho = 0$ [zofka2008, lemos1995].
Written in horospherical coordinates, this black hole shares the leading terms of the field far from the axis when $\Lambda < 0$, and the radial dependence of its next terms [zofka2008].
Every member with $\Lambda < 0$ approaches anti-de Sitter space far from its axis, in horospherical coordinates [dasilva2000, zofka2008].

When $\Lambda > 0$, a toroidal region of the static universe full of dust can replace one of the two singular axes, and for small $\sigma$ the dust carries a mass per unit length close to $\sigma$ [griffiths2010linettian].

The member with $\sigma = 0$ is a generalisation of the B III metric with a cosmological constant, of type D and in the family of Jerzy Plebański and Marek Demiański without expansion [griffiths2010linettian].

coordinates.name: Toroidal

parameters.description: Cosmological constant, positive here, an inverse length squared
Conicity about the axis $\rho = \pi/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$, dimensionless; with $\psi$ periodic in $2\pi$ it fixes the angular deficit there
Conicity, dimensionless; with $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$ it fixes the angular deficit about the axis, which at $\sigma = 0$ is $2\pi(1 - 1/C)$
Exponent along $t$, $p_0 = 2\sigma/\Sigma$, with $\sigma$ the mass parameter of Levi-Civita's cylinder and $\Sigma = 4\sigma^2 - 2\sigma + 1$
Exponent along $\phi$, $p_2 = (1 - 2\sigma)/\Sigma$
Exponent along $\psi$, $p_3 = 2\sigma(2\sigma - 1)/\Sigma$; the two conditions on the exponents leave one free
A length, close to $\rho$ near the axis and growing without bound as $\rho \to \pi/\sqrt{3\Lambda}$, with $dP/d\rho = 1 + 3\Lambda P^2/4$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, \psi, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $\rho$ the proper distance from the axis $\rho = 0$, a length, and $\psi$ and $\phi$ angles. The factor $(1 + 3\Lambda P^2/4)^{-2/3}$ is $\cos^{4/3}(\sqrt{3\Lambda}\,\rho/2)$, and we evaluate the powers of $P$ with $P$ in a fixed unit of length, so they are dimensionless. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Cylindrical

parameters.description: Cosmological constant, negative here, an inverse length squared
Conicity, dimensionless; with $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$ it fixes the angular deficit about the axis, which at $\sigma = 0$ is $2\pi(1 - 1/C)$
Exponent along $t$, $p_0 = 2\sigma/\Sigma$, with $\sigma$ the mass parameter of Levi-Civita's cylinder and $\Sigma = 4\sigma^2 - 2\sigma + 1$
Exponent along $\phi$, $p_2 = (1 - 2\sigma)/\Sigma$
Exponent along $z$, $p_3 = 2\sigma(2\sigma - 1)/\Sigma$; the two conditions on the exponents leave one free
A length, close to $\rho$ near the axis and tending to $2/\sqrt{-3\Lambda}$ far from it, with $dP/d\rho = 1 + 3\Lambda P^2/4$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, z, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\rho$, the proper distance from the axis, and $z$ lengths. The factor $(1 + 3\Lambda P^2/4)^{-2/3}$ is $\cosh^{4/3}(\sqrt{-3\Lambda}\,\rho/2)$, and we evaluate the powers of $P$ with $P$ in a fixed unit of length, so they are dimensionless. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Gleiser

parameters.description: Cosmological constant, of either sign, an inverse length squared
Conicity, dimensionless; with $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$ it fixes the angular deficit about the axis, which at $\sigma = 0$ is $2\pi(1 - 1/C)$
Exponent along $t$, $p_0 = 2\sigma/\Sigma$, with $\sigma$ the mass parameter of Levi-Civita's cylinder and $\Sigma = 4\sigma^2 - 2\sigma + 1$
Exponent along $\phi$, $p_2 = (1 - 2\sigma)/\Sigma$
Exponent along $z$, $p_3 = 2\sigma(2\sigma - 1)/\Sigma$; the two conditions on the exponents leave one free

coordinates.convention: We use Gleiser's coordinates $(t, y, z, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $z$ a length and $\Lambda y = \sin^2(\sqrt{3\Lambda}\,\rho/2)$, where $\rho$ is the proper distance from the axis, so that $t$, $z$ and $\phi/C$ are those of the proper distance charts multiplied by constants. We evaluate the powers of $y$ and of $1 - \Lambda y$ with lengths in a fixed unit, so they are dimensionless. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Sarıoğlu-Tekin

parameters.description: Radius of anti-de Sitter space, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$
Value of $r$ on the axis, a length
Conicity, dimensionless; with $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$ it fixes the angular deficit about the axis, which at $\sigma = 0$ is $2\pi(1 - 1/C)$
Exponent along $t$, $p_0 = 2\sigma/\Sigma$, with $\sigma$ the mass parameter of Levi-Civita's cylinder and $\Sigma = 4\sigma^2 - 2\sigma + 1$
Exponent along $\phi$, $p_2 = (1 - 2\sigma)/\Sigma$
Exponent along $z$, $p_3 = 2\sigma(2\sigma - 1)/\Sigma$; the two conditions on the exponents leave one free
Dimensionless, rising from $0$ on the axis to $1$ far from it, with $dh/dr = 3(1 - h)/r$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, r, z, \phi)$ of Sarıoğlu and Tekin, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ and $z$ lengths, where $r = r_0\cosh^{2/3}(3\rho/2L)$ with $\rho$ the proper distance from the axis, so that $t$, $z$ and $\phi/C$ are those of the cylindrical chart multiplied by constants. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
